name: Parametric IACC symmetric spinnaker series (Moore / Lasher-Richards), five sails of the same girth

source.citation: Moore P. (2004). Numerical modelling of a series of parametric spinnakers. ME thesis, University of Auckland. Lasher W. C., Richards P. J. (2007). Validation of Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes simulations for international America's Cup class spinnaker force coefficients in an atmospheric boundary layer. Journal of Ship Research 51(1), 22-38. Equations and coefficients as reprinted in Peart T. (2022), PhD thesis, University of Auckland, appendix A, https://researchspace.auckland.ac.nz/handle/2292/64018.
source.licence: published equations and coefficients (facts, not a copyrighted work); cited
source.method: rigid 1:25 wind-tunnel models of an IACC symmetric spinnaker in closed form; the five sails share the girth and differ mainly in how far apart the clews are (foot camber 23.0, 28.5, 34.8, 39.8, 44.6 %)
source.sail: luff 1.30 m and about 0.8 m2 at model scale (about 32 m and 500 m2 at 1:25)

definitions.surface: x = kx * sum(n=0..4) (a_n s^3 + b_n s) t^n (lateral, luff to luff), y = ky (t - 0.1) (up), z = kz * sum(n=0..3) (c_n s^2 + d_n) t^n (the belly's side), s from -0.5 to 0.5, t from 0.1 (the foot) to where the luffs meet (the head)
definitions.shapes: flatter on a reach, deeper running: sail I at AWA 60 to sail V dead downwind, neighbours blended; the dead-run sail projected forward as a running kite flies (run_bow, a share of the luff at mid height) with its clew eased forward (clew_ease, deg at the foot)
